# DG FISMA — Directorate-General for Financial Stability, Financial Services and Capital Markets Union

> Supports the Commissioner for Financial Services and the Savings and Investments Union (`financial-services`), guided by the Executive Vice-President for Prosperity and Industrial Strategy. Roster: `knowledge/roster.yml`.

---

## Institutional role

DG FISMA writes the EU's financial-sector rulebook: banking, insurance, capital markets, payments, crypto-assets, sustainable finance and anti-money laundering. It drives the Savings and Investments Union, oversees the European Supervisory Authorities' rule-making through delegated and implementing acts, and works with the ECB on the Banking Union. Supervision itself sits with the ECB (significant banks), the ESAs, the Single Resolution Board, AMLA and national authorities.

---

## Main areas of work

| Area | Content |
|---|---|
| Savings and Investments Union | Capital-markets integration, supervision, retail investment, pensions |
| Banking | Prudential rules (CRR/CRD, Basel III), resolution and deposit insurance, Banking Union completion |
| Capital markets | MiFID II/MiFIR, market infrastructure (EMIR), securitisation, listing |
| Insurance and pensions | Solvency II, IORP, supplementary pensions |
| Sustainable finance | Taxonomy, SFDR, green bonds |
| Digital finance and payments | MiCA, DORA, instant payments, payment services, financial data access |
| Financial crime | AML package and the Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA) |

---

| Instrument | Legal basis |

| Capital Requirements Regulation and Directive | Reg. 575/2013 and Dir. 2013/36/EU, as amended |
| Bank Recovery and Resolution Directive; Single Resolution Mechanism | Dir. 2014/59/EU; Reg. 806/2014 |
| MiFID II / MiFIR | Dir. 2014/65/EU; Reg. 600/2014 |
| Solvency II | Dir. 2009/138/EC |
| Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) | Reg. 2023/1114 |
| Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) | Reg. 2022/2554 |
| AML package and AMLA | Reg. 2024/1624; Dir. 2024/1640; Reg. 2024/1620 |
| Taxonomy Regulation; SFDR | Reg. 2020/852; Reg. 2019/2088 |
| European Supervisory Authorities | Regs. 1093/2010 (EBA), 1094/2010 (EIOPA), 1095/2010 (ESMA) |

---

## Legal basis

- **Internal market:** Art. 114 TFEU, the basis of most financial regulation
- **Establishment and services:** Art. 53(1) TFEU (taking up and pursuit of activities)
- **Capital movements:** Arts. 63–66 TFEU
- **ECB supervision:** Art. 127(6) TFEU (Council unanimity, special legislative procedure)
- **Digital euro:** Art. 133 TFEU, with DG ECFIN in the lead

---

## ISC behavior

When DG FISMA participates in an inter-service consultation, it:
- Checks the effect on financial stability, market integration and the cost of capital.
- Flags new reporting or disclosure duties for financial firms and their overlap with existing rules.
- Checks consistency with the Single Rulebook and the ESAs' powers (Meroni limits on delegation to agencies).
- Raises AML and sanctions-compliance angles in payment or crypto-related files.
- Asks whether the measure helps or hinders the Savings and Investments Union.

---

## Structural tensions

| Counterpart | Nature of tension |
|---|---|
| DG ECFIN | Digital euro design and banks' funding; financial stability vs. growth |
| DG COMP | State aid to banks; competition in payments |
| DG JUST | Consumer protection in retail finance; company law and sustainability due diligence |
| DG CLIMA / DG ENV | Ambition of sustainable-finance rules vs. simplification for preparers |
| DG CNECT | Financial data access and digital identity; big tech in finance |
| ECB | Prudential calibration (Basel III output floor, market risk) and supervisory centralisation |

## Output standards

DG FISMA outputs must:
- Name the supervisory authority that will apply the rule (ECB, ESA, SRB, AMLA, national).
- Distinguish level 1 legislation from delegated and implementing acts and ESA technical standards.
- State the financial-stability and cost-of-capital effects.
